reviews.review:
Banzai Escape is a Rail Shooter by Xenoaisam, a guy who was known at one point for making custom anime-themed models for gamers and he had a bit of a following for players in the Obsidian Conflict and/or Garry's Mod communities. Some of the models he's made are ones of his own original characters and universe. Banzai Escape is part of that universe with the protoganist being his character Rokiahi whose objective as an operative of PASKAL is to raid Amino Corp (which is said to have ties to the terrorist organization SPECTRE) and capture it's founder Asword Betas all the while shooting your way through various bad guys including the forces of SPECTRE themselves and/or the security personnel of Amino Corp.

Now gameplay-wise it reminds me of the shooting-gallery-esque minigames in Star Wars: Rebel Assault II - Rebel Strike in that you are only able to switch cover positions whenever you can or take cover while gunning down enemies. You start off with an SMG and a pistol but after getting past the first actual level you can buy some better weapons using money you get off dead enemies. A majority of them are fire-arms but if you get past the final boss you'll be able to get an energy weapon if you have the money for it. Most of the enemies you'll face at first are some grunts armed with various guns ranging from pistols to shotguns to assault rifles but you'll occasionally have to deal with grunts wielding riot shields, grunts throwing grenades, and flying drones armed with machine guns. The bosses can be a bit challenging though if you memorize the patterns in which they attack and if you're using one of the upper-tier weapons than fighting them will be a piece of cake. 

The levels are decent in terms of combat and navigation but the environments remind me a lot of some of neo-futuristic locales in anime/manga such Academy City from Toaru Kagaku No Railgun/A Certain Scientific Railgun and to some extent some of the cities in the Pokemon animated series. This style can also be seen with the graphic design work done for the GUI and/or the HUD. 

Originally, the dialogue was full of grammatical and/or spelling errors but this has largely been corrected by Xenoaisam with some help from some of his friends, fans, and associates. Other than that though my only major gripe is that the system that is used to buy weapons and ammunition because you need to buy a ♥♥♥♥ ton of ammo for whichever primary weapon you plan on using because otherwise you could end up being reduced to your pistol without enough ammo to keep you locked and loaded throughout the level. Thankfully, Xenoaisam has plans to fix and/or improve it for Banzai Escape Ep.2. 

All in all, its not a bad start for the Banzai Escape series but once again I do believe that this game along with its sequel(s) have room for improvement especially in terms of some of the gameplay and/or game mechanics.

6.5/10

The only real fault of this on-rails shooter is being overly ambitious. The shooting controls are tight. There's plenty of fire-arms to try out. And the character customization, no matter how limited, is always a welcome touch. Where the game falls flat is when you must utilize its more unintuitive controls. There are brief, almost mini-game like segments where you must jump over, duck, and sidestep environmental hazards by using your mouse's directional inputs. It's laggy, inelegant, and can easily end an otherwise perfect run.

Nevertheless, I maintain there is far more right than wrong with "Banzai Escape." If you can overlook a few rough spots meant to break up the monotony of blowing away anything that moves, there's a lot of fun to be had in this arcade blast-a-thon. If you're already curious about this title, I doubt it will leave you feeling disappointed. Give it a try.
